name: go-tasks
requirements: T1 core/task.go, package core: the task model, its store and the clock. Task is struct { ID int; Title string; Due time.Time; Repeat string; Tags []string; Done bool }; Due is a UTC midnight, or the zero time when the task has no due date. Clock is interface { Now() time.Time }. Day(t time.Time) time.Time returns the UTC midnight that starts t's UTC date. NewStore() *Store returns an empty in-memory store. (*Store).Add(t Task) (Task, error) normalizes t, gives it the next ID, stores it and returns the stored task. IDs are 1, 2, 3 and so on in the order of successful adds, whatever t.ID holds; a failed add uses no ID. Normalizing trims the title with strings.TrimSpace and fails if it is then empty; replaces a nonzero Due with Day(Due); trims and lowercases each tag, failing if a tag is then empty or holds any character other than a-z, 0-9 and -; and sorts the tags and drops duplicates. Repeat and Done are stored as given. (*Store).Get(id int) (Task, bool) returns the task with that ID and whether it exists. (*Store).Update(t Task) error normalizes t the same way and replaces the stored task that has t's ID; it fails, changing nothing, when no task has that ID or normalizing fails. (*Store).All() []Task returns every stored task in ascending ID order. The store shares no memory with its callers: changing a Task or Tags slice passed to Add or Update, or returned by Add, Get or All, never changes the store.

T2 commands.go, package tasks (the module's root package): the command dispatch table. Env is struct { Store *core.Store; Clock core.Clock }. Args is struct { Flags map[string]string; Words []string }. Command is func(env Env, args Args) (string, error). var commands = map[string]Command{...} is the dispatch table from a command's name to its Command, and Run finds commands only there. ParseArgs(words []string) (Args, error): a word starting with -- is a flag whose name is the rest of the word and whose value is the next word, whatever that word is; every other word goes to Words in order. Flags is never nil. An empty flag name (the word --), a flag with no next word or a repeated flag name is an error. Run(env Env, words []string) (string, error) fails when words is empty or words[0] is not in commands; otherwise it parses words[1:] with ParseArgs and returns what that command returns. Put two commands in the table. add: its Words joined by single spaces are the title, with optional flags --due DATE (a valid YYYY-MM-DD date, as time.Parse reads it with time.DateOnly), --tags LIST (split at commas into Tags) and --every RULE (stored in Repeat as given); any other flag is an error. It stores the task with Store.Add, returning Add's error, and prints "added #ID\n". done: exactly one word, the decimal ID of a stored task that is not done, and no flags; it sets the task's Done with Store.Update and prints "done #ID\n". Anything else is an error.

T3 due/due.go, package due: relative due dates. With today = core.Day(clock.Now()), Parse(spec string, clock core.Clock) (time.Time, error) accepts exactly one of these forms and returns a UTC midnight: today; tomorrow; +Nd and +Nw, N days or N weeks after today, where N is one to three ASCII digits; mon, tue, wed, thu, fri, sat and sun, the first date after today that falls on that weekday (on a Wednesday, wed is a week ahead); and a valid YYYY-MM-DD date, as time.Parse reads it with time.DateOnly. Anything else is an error, including capitals and surrounding spaces. Window(filter string, clock core.Clock) (from, to time.Time, err error) returns the range of due dates that a list filter selects, from being the first date it selects: overdue selects the due dates before today, with from the zero time; today selects today; week selects today and the six days after it. Any other filter is an error. A task with no due date is in no window.

T4 recur/recur.go, package recur: recurrence rules. Parse(text string) (Rule, error) accepts exactly daily, weekly, monthly, weekdays, and "every N UNIT": the word every, N and a UNIT of day, days, week, weeks, month or months, separated by single spaces, where N is a positive decimal integer with no sign and no leading zeros. daily is every 1 day, weekly is every 1 week and monthly is every 1 month. Anything else is an error. (Rule).Next(date time.Time) time.Time returns a UTC midnight, the next occurrence after core.Day(date): every N days adds N days and every N weeks adds 7N days; every N months gives the same day of the month N months later, or that month's last day when it is shorter (monthly after 2026-01-31 is 2026-02-28); weekdays gives the first later date that is a Monday to Friday. Advance(t core.Task) (core.Task, error) returns t's next occurrence: a copy of t with ID 0, Done false and Due set to Next(t.Due) for the rule in t.Repeat, sharing no Tags memory with t. It fails when t.Repeat does not parse or t has no due date.

T5 query/query.go, package query: the tag query language. Parse(text string) (Query, error) parses a query, and (Query).Match(t core.Task) bool reports whether t.Tags satisfy it. Whitespace separates tokens, and ( and ) are tokens of their own even with no space around them. and, or and not are keywords. Every other token is a pattern: a tag (one or more of a-z, 0-9 and -), which matches a task that has exactly that tag, or a tag prefix followed by *, which matches a task that has a tag starting with that prefix; the prefix may be empty, so * matches a task with any tag. The grammar, loosest first: query = term { or term }; term = factor { [and] factor }, so two factors with no keyword between them are joined by and; factor = not factor | ( query ) | pattern. Anything else is an error: no tokens, a keyword where a pattern belongs, unbalanced parentheses, or any other character.

T6 export/export.go, package export: CSV export. CSV(tasks []core.Task) string writes, with encoding/csv's Writer (comma separator, \n line ends), a header row id,title,due,repeat,tags,done and then one row per task in the order given: the ID in decimal, the title, the due date as YYYY-MM-DD or empty when there is none, Repeat, the tags joined by single spaces, and Done as true or false.

T7 list.go, package tasks: the list command. Add "list": list to commands. list takes no words and only the flags --status, --tag and --due; anything else is an error. --status is open (the default: the tasks not done), done or all. --tag QUERY keeps the tasks that query.Parse(QUERY) matches; a query that does not parse is an error. --due FILTER is none, keeping the tasks with no due date, or a filter of due.Window(FILTER, env.Clock), keeping the tasks whose due date is in that window; any other filter is an error, even when no task would print. A task prints when it passes every flag given. Tasks with a due date come first, by due date, then the tasks without one; ties go by ID. Each task is one line: [ ] for an open task or [x] for a done one, a space, #ID, a space and the title; then " due:YYYY-MM-DD" when it has a due date, and " +TAG" for each tag in order; then \n. When no task is selected, list prints nothing.

T8 report.go, package tasks: the report command. Add "report": report to commands. report takes no words and only the flag --tag QUERY, which limits the report to the tasks that query.Parse(QUERY) matches (all tasks without it); anything else is an error. An open task is overdue when its due date is in due.Window("overdue", env.Clock); a done task is never overdue. For each tag that a counted task has, in ascending order, report prints "TAG: O open, V overdue, D done\n", where O counts the open tasks with that tag, V the overdue ones among them and D the done ones; then "TOTAL: O open, V overdue, D done\n" over every counted task, tagged or not. Cross-ticket requirement, T7 and T8: report's counts agree with what list's filters show. With the same --tag flag, or none, the TOTAL line's O, V and D are the numbers of tasks that list, list --due overdue and list --status done print, and each tag's line gives the same numbers when the query also requires that tag.

allocation.A: T1, T3, T4 and T7: core/task.go, due/due.go, recur/recur.go and list.go, with focused tests.
allocation.B: T2, T5, T6 and T8: commands.go, query/query.go, export/export.go and report.go, with focused tests.

dependencies: Packages: core imports no package of the module; due, recur, query and export import only core; the root package tasks imports them all.
T2 uses T1's Task, Store and Clock.
T3, T4, T5 and T6 each sit in their own package and need only T1: T3 uses Clock and Day, T4 uses Day and Task, and T5 and T6 use Task.
T7 uses T2's Env, Args and commands, T3's due.Window, and T5's query.Parse and Query.Match.
T8 uses T2's Env, Args and commands, T3's due.Window, and T5's query.Parse and Query.Match.
T7 and T8 each add one entry to commands, and T8's counts must agree with T7's list (T8's cross-ticket requirement).
